question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese smaller possessions and their geographic locations]
options: Mozambique Island – East African coast, present-day Mozambique
Mombasa (Fort Jesus) – East African coast, present-day Kenya
Macau – South China coast, near the Pearl River Delta
Timor – Island in the South China Sea, east of Philippines
wrong_fact: Timor is located in the Lesser Sunda Islands of Southeast Asia, in the Timor Sea between Australia and Indonesia — NOT in the South China Sea east of the Philippines.
explanation: Timor (Portuguese Timor, now East Timor/Timor-Leste) is situated in the eastern Indonesian archipelago, between the Timor Sea and the Banda Sea, south of Flores and west of Papua. It is far from the Philippines. Mozambique Island was a key Portuguese East African base; Fort Jesus at Mombasa controlled the East African coast; and Macau on the South China coast was Portugal's key China trading post.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese East African forts/bases and the rival power that displaced them]
options: Fort Jesus, Mombasa – Captured by Omani Arabs in 1698
Kilwa (Tanzania) – Portuguese displaced by Zimba people and later Omani Arabs
Mombasa – Lost by Portuguese to the Dutch East India Company in 1698
wrong_fact: Fort Jesus at Mombasa was captured in 1698 by the Omani Arabs (from the Sultanate of Oman), NOT by the Dutch East India Company. The Dutch were primarily active in Southeast Asia and Ceylon, not East Africa.
explanation: The Omani Arabs (Yarubi dynasty of Oman) besieged Fort Jesus at Mombasa for 33 months and finally captured it in December 1698, marking the end of Portuguese control over East Africa north of Mozambique. The Dutch were not involved in East African campaigns. Mozambique Island remained Portuguese until Mozambican independence in 1975. Kilwa had been seized and held intermittently by Portugal before Arab resurgence.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Estado da India (smaller Indian possessions) and their current status]
options: Daman (Damão) – Annexed by India in 1961, now part of Daman and Diu UT
Diu – Island at the tip of Kathiawar/Saurashtra Peninsula, Gujarat
Dadra and Nagar Haveli – Inland enclaves in Gujarat, integrated into India in 1954
São Tomé de Meliapor (Mylapore) – Retained by Portugal until 1961 as part of Estado da India
wrong_fact: São Tomé de Meliapor (Mylapore, near Madras/Chennai) was NOT retained by Portugal until 1961. It was captured by the Dutch in 1662 and later came under British control, becoming part of Madras Presidency long before Indian independence.
explanation: São Tomé de Meliapor (Mylapore) near present-day Chennai was a Portuguese settlement famous as the site of St. Thomas's tomb. It was seized by the Dutch in 1662, then by the British, and became part of Madras Presidency — it was never part of the Estado da India that persisted until 1961. The possessions that India annexed in 1961 were Goa, Daman, and Diu. Dadra and Nagar Haveli were liberated by Indian irregular forces in 1954.
